zones.note: Lexical review aid: NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, version 202510, CC BY 4.0. Source: https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html ; license: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ . Consulted after independent scan reading; the diplomatic readings and English notes here are reviewer-authored, not an imported transcription.

runs.text: custureira, ou bom official de mãos, ou bõ frẽ-

lines.note: Continues the preceding page's hand-skill definition: a good seamstress, manual craftsperson, or archer. The faint nasal mark in bõ is retained; the archer-word continues below.
Completes the archer-word and introduces te no kiita saiku, a skilled craftsperson. The Portuguese explanation runs onto the next row.
Finishes the dexterous-craftsperson gloss, then begins an example about someone with a good sense of rhythm. No hyphen is supplied after fi.
To completes hito. The Portuguese describes a well-timed performer; bem corrects OCR hem, while the printed single-s compaſado is retained.

runs.text: do tom no bailar, tanger, cantar, &c.

lines.note: Completes the rhythm example with dancing, instrumental playing, and singing without departing from the proper measure or tone.
Kusuri ga kiku means a medicine takes effect, demonstrating a sense of kiku other than hearing.
Kaji ga kikanu describes a vessel failing to respond to its rudder. The article a is separated from the divided embarcação.
Completes the rudder example and begins successful hunting or fishing, whose Portuguese object follows below.

runs.text: boa caça, ou peſcaria tomando algũa couſa.

lines.note: Explains success as actually catching something while hunting or fishing; the source's broad sense is preserved.
Describes a person successful in the hunt; the relative clause is completed on the next physical row.
Finishes the successful-hunter example and begins another involving favorable dice throws.

runs.text: Homem que deita bem os dados ou lhe

lines.note: Hito completes the Japanese phrase; the Portuguese describes someone who casts dice successfully or gets favorable results.

runs.text: ſae ſempre como deſeja. ¶ Item, per met.

lines.note: Completes the desired-results explanation and explicitly introduces a metaphorical extension with per met.

runs.text: Homem bem afortunado, ou que ſempre ganha

lines.note: The figurative meaning is a fortunate person who consistently gains or wins; the field of activity follows below.
Completes the favorable-fortune sense with success in trade and other matters.
Introduces the noun kiki, hearing, with an example about how a name sounds. The broad initial Q is not a separate word.

runs.text: Eſte nome ſoa bem nos ouuidos.

lines.note: Completes kono na wa kiki ga yoi: the name sounds pleasant to the ears.
Kikiawase is comparing or checking by listening. The printed principal ending ſuru is retained rather than regularized from a modern conjugation.
Kiki ayamari introduces mishearing or misunderstanding what is said. The source separates the two Japanese components.

runs.text: ſe diz, ou ouuir hũa couſa por outra.

lines.note: Completes the definition as hearing one thing in place of another.
The verb kikichigae likewise means mishearing. Qiqi replaces the malformed OCR Quqi, supported directly by the repeated form below.
Completes the verb's explanation, hearing one thing for another; it remains a separate short continuation.

runs.text: O ouuir hũa couſa por outra.

lines.note: Gives the corresponding noun for mishearing, separately from the preceding verb and its principal forms.

runs.text: Couſa que ſe entende mal, ou que

lines.note: Describes something difficult to understand by hearing. The opening Q is restored; the historical douoi spelling is not modernized.
Completes the difficult-hearing definition as something not clearly perceived or understood.

runs.text: Com ocaſião de ouuir, ou pera ouuir.

lines.note: Kikigatera means on the occasion of hearing or in order to hear. The extra u in OCR Quiqigatera is absent from the scan.
Describes something pleasant or gratifying to hear, not simply any audible matter.

Kiki idashi concerns happening to hear or discovering through hearing. The damaged d is supported by the repeated example and NINJAL; a second-pass comparison resolves two u types in Portuguese ouuir, not an internal t.
Completes the discovery gloss and starts a quotation about the Heike. The Japanese example begins after italic Vt.

runs.text: axij ſamani mǒſu monoga araba, ichinin

lines.note: Continues the conditional quotation: should someone speak badly of the Heike, the question is whether anyone hears of it.
Completes the quotation's negative hearing condition. Feiq. is the upright citation label, not part of the Japanese sentence.

runs.text: Lib. 1. Auendo alguem que falaſſe mal do

lines.note: Identifies book 1 and begins the Portuguese rendering of someone speaking ill of the Heike. The scan supports two long-s strokes in falaſſe.

runs.text: Feique, em quanto hum não acertaua de ouuir

lines.note: Continues the translation: the speaker remained safe while nobody happened to hear. Feique is an embedded Japanese name; the garbled one-letter typeface split is removed.
Concludes the translation by saying that the absence of a hearer served the speaker well.
Kiki ire means giving ear or admitting something. The Portuguese admitir begins at the right edge.
Completes admitir, gives mimi ni kiki iruru as the same expression, and introduces a literary example.

runs.text: Xôxôno togauoba miminimo qiqi ire ta-

lines.note: Begins an honorific statement about not giving ear even to minor faults. The final verb is physically divided after ta-.
Completes tamawazu and gives the printed upright citation label Taif. The Portuguese translation begins 'not a single' and continues below; the label is not silently expanded or respelled.
Finishes the translation as neither hearing nor admitting even the smallest fault.
Kikin denotes general famine, explained through hunger. The initial Q replaces OCR g, and the example begins the same word across the line break.
Completes the example about a famine occurring, with Portuguese Auer retained in its historical spelling.
Kikinarai means learning by hearing. The printed spacing a prender is provisionally retained rather than silently regularized to aprender.
Kikinareru means becoming accustomed to hearing. The Portuguese spelling Acustumar is preserved.
Kikinashi concerns interpreting what one hears in a particular way. Cousa continues below without a supplied hyphen.

runs.text: ſa em boa, ou em mà parte.

lines.note: Completes the interpretation as taking something in a good or bad sense; the grave in mà is preserved.
Kikinaoshi means hearing or construing something afresh. Second-pass comparison with adjacent ouuir forms establishes two u types here, correcting the draft's shorter reading.

runs.text: ſa differentemente do que ſe tinha ouuido.

lines.note: Completes the definition as hearing something differently from before. Two f types are visible in differentemente, correcting the draft's single f.

runs.text: Fugir ſoo com a fama dos inimigos.

lines.note: Kikinige means fleeing merely on hearing reports of the enemy. The g in nigue is visible, replacing the OCR's ç.
Gives kikinige wo suru as the illustrative expression. Q belongs to the upright Japanese word, not to italic Vt or a separate O.
Kikinuki means hearing something properly through to the end. The printed shorter past ending uita is retained.
Begins the example of hearing out another person's thoughts or opinion; the Portuguese translation continues below.
Completes the example as hearing someone's opinion carefully and completely.

Cayeru saru explains returning or going away, with the destination continued below. The faint trace between e and u supports r on enlargement, so Cayeru is retained rather than the first-pass Cayeu; the abraded r remains a local caveat.
Completes the homeward-return definition with 'one's own house'.
Kyō e kaeru explains returning to the capital. The apparent italic O in the draft is actually the initial Q of Qiǒye; Miaco is embedded in Portuguese.
Okite iru means being up or risen. The unmarked-o headword differs from the preceding return-to-capital entry; the source spacing a leuantado is retained.
Gives a mirror and, by extension, a good model or example, with Qiqei as an alternative form.
Begins an example about learning from virtuous people. Initial I in Iennin has the dictionary's consonantal value; it is not replaced by modern J or Z.
Bu completes manabu, and the Portuguese translates the example as imitating holy or virtuous people.

runs.text: Hũa erua, ou flor, & araiz da meſ-

lines.note: Introduces kikyō as an herb, its flower, and its root. The attached araiz and divided meſma are retained as printed.
Completes the plant description and introduces kikyō-iro, the flower's color.

runs.text: q̃ he en tre azul, & roxo. ¶ Item, Hũa me-

lines.note: Places the flower's color between blue and purple, then starts a medicinal sense. The unusual printed en tre spacing is retained.

runs.text: zinha que ſe faz da raiz deſta erua.

lines.note: Completes mezinha and explains that the medicine is made from the plant's root.
Kiki sadame concerns determining a matter through hearing. The headword's printed internal space is preserved.

runs.text: nar, ou confirmarſe no que ouuio.

lines.note: Completes determinar and adds becoming certain of what one has heard.
Kiki sumashi concerns attentive or complete hearing; the Portuguese qualification follows on the next row.
Specifies hearing well and thoroughly, completing the preceding entry rather than introducing another example.
Kikisute is not hearing a matter out, especially through disregard. The Portuguese verb is physically divided.

runs.text: uir, como fazendo pouco caſo da couſa.

lines.note: Completes the gloss by explaining that the listener makes little of the matter.
Kikitate means hearing by making inquiries or obtaining information. The Portuguese reflexive phrase continues below.

runs.text: ſe do q̃ paßa, como o que ouuio algũa conjura

lines.note: Describes learning what is happening, with a conspiracy as the first example. Conjuração is divided without an added hyphen.

runs.text: ção ainda encuberta, ou o lugar onde algum la-

lines.note: Completes the concealed-conspiracy example and begins another about a thief's hiding place.
Completes ladrão and the example of finding out where a thief has hidden.
Kikitsukuroi likewise concerns hearing and informing oneself. Both printed long-vowel marks in the abbreviated principal forms are circumflexes.

runs.text: ſe do que paßa, ou do modo, &c.

lines.note: Completes the definition as learning what happens or how it happens.

runs.text: Ouuir de nouo o que não

lines.note: Kikitsuke begins with the sense of newly hearing something previously unknown. Ouuir replaces the malformed OCR Ouair.

runs.text: ſabia, ou eſtaua encuberto. ¶ Item, Cuſ-

lines.note: Completes the hidden-or-unknown sense and starts another: becoming accustomed to hearing something.
Completes custumar-se and introduces an example about a familiar matter one has heard before.

runs.text: He couſa que estou cuſtumado a ouuir.

lines.note: Gia completes the Japanese assertion; the Portuguese confirms that this is something the speaker is accustomed to hearing.
Kikitogame means noticing or taking exception while hearing. The headword's initial Q is restored from the OCR's italic O.
Kikitogime is a separate entry for hearing properly and completely. Its printed gi is not changed to match the preceding game form.
Completes inteiramente, emphasizing completeness of hearing.
Kikitoori is hearing everything. The historical ou sequence and abbreviated inflectional forms are preserved.
Kikitooshi means hearing through to the end. The scan has Ouuir with two u types and the attached ocabo.
Kikiwake concerns discriminating or understanding through hearing, rather than merely receiving sound.
Completes the definition as understanding the matter heard.
Kiki wakimae is assigned the same meaning as kikiwake. The printed internal space remains.
Kikiotoshi means missing something in hearing. The scan's v replaces OCR r, with the corrected headword also supported by NINJAL.

runs.text: por ouuir, ou deixar de ou. algũa couſa.

lines.note: Explains leaving something unheard. The visibly shortened ou. is retained rather than editorially expanded to ouuir; its damaged following punctuation is not treated as missing words.
Kikioyobi is hearing from afar or coming to hear of something. The opening Q replaces the OCR's detached lowercase o.

runs.text: ou vir à noticia dalgũa couſa.

lines.note: Adds coming to knowledge of a matter; the grave in à is preserved.
Kikishiri means knowing by hearing, with a further sense concerning understanding speech.
Completes entender and specifies a foreign language, then starts a quotation about not understanding spoken words.
Completes kotoba mo kikishirazu and gives the upright Heike citation label with italic book reference. The Portuguese translation begins on the following page; Nem below is a catchword.
